To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Web can be a platform for e‐books and that it can be used to implement the most advanced features that are desirable in this area.

the Web is the ideal medium for electronic books if the Web is enhanced by a set of standards and technologies for client‐side adaptation, and if the Web is used as a content delivery platform that supports advanced browsing functionalities.
e‐books can be implemented in the Web context and that they can be made device independent and adaptive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an e‐book format and with the implementation of advanced browsing functionalities for e‐books on the WWW.
the development of an XML‐based e‐book format that is device independent and that can be browsed on the Web.
the design of a new generation of electronic books that can take full advantage of the World Wide Web and its standards.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
e‐books are a viable option, but that they will only be competitive when they are Web‐based, device‐independent, and adaptive.
the future for e‐books on the Web is bright.
the WWW is a promising basis for the development and dissemination of electronic books.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Web is not a good platform for e‐books because of its lack of support for adaptive presentation and device independence, but that the Web can be improved to support e‐books better.
the WWW is not yet a suitable platform for e‐book publishing, but that the proposed enhancements could make it a good platform for a future generation of e‐book systems.

e‐book publishing is a promising field of application for the WWW, and that a few extensions to the current WWW standards are needed in order to make e‐book publishing more attractive and more efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the Web age, e‐books are not a separate medium but an extension of Web‐based publishing.
the Web can be a good platform for e‐books if the Web standards are enhanced in the directions we have suggested.
e‐books can compete with paper books in the WWW age, provided that they offer a better user experience.
